He told me to go and see Toso Pajic because there are some dead bodies kind of buried around. I went to see Toso Pajic and he referred me to Djuro Skaljac, his second in command. We then picked up, I believe, two prisoners - they were both Croatian nationals - took me outside of Vojnic to a little deserted place by the river there and pointed out to the area when these two Croatian nationals should start digging. They dig out -- they did dig out four bodies. The problem that I had with them, first they were in a high state of decomposition, so it was not something that happened recently in a combat situation. Obviously they were there for a considerable number of months. And the second even more worrying thing was that all four bodies had their hands tied with wire up front, which would suggest they were executed, that they did not actually die in a combat situation. But being pressed for the bodies, nevertheless I took those four, removed the wire, and put them in the body bags.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you obtain another 90 bodies from other graves in the area?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir, but those are the known gravesites of the real combat members of the 5th Corps that were killed in recent actions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, even with this 90 plus four bodies, did you still need to identify or secure six other additional bodies for the exchange?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: General agreement between the 5th Corps and the 39th Corps was one for one, meaning as many as we offered, that's how many we're going to get, one for one sort of a thing. So it was still six short.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go -- did you at some point -- or at some point were you directed to speak to one of Arkan's Tigers regarding securing six more bodies?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was directed to go there by Colonel Karan Mlado, who was internal security officer for the 21st Corps, and he usually would have information where the people were held as prisoners or people being shot or something like that. So he directed me to go to Pauk command and speak to Colonel Bozovic and Colonel Pejovic. One was the MUP Serbia -- Bozovic was MUP Serbia, and Pejovic was Arkan's Tigers. See if they can assist.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened when you spoke to Pejovic?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I spoke first to Bozovic and Bozovic told me if you need dead. You go and fight and bring your own dead. So that was a very brief meeting. He wouldn't help us in this matter no matter how much I pleaded with him. I wasn't doing this for myself; you know, for the families. Then I was sent then to go to separate like a little subcommand, if you like, where Colonel Pejovic was, and then he sent me to his second in command, Captain Sarac, who calmly said he doesn't have any dead bodies however he does have six live ones and I can have them if I need them badly enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: The whole commission just turned around and walked away. We drove back and then we were told to come back the following morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you go back to Captain Sarac the next morning?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: We went back to the Pauk command which told us there are bodies ready for us, as Captain Sarac commanded. We went there and there were six dead bodies lined up which appeared to be very freshly killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "freshly killed," did it appear to you that they had been killed in the period since you last left the Pauk command?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I would say they were killed about an hour before we came the second time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Again, these bodies now were too fresh compared to all the other bodies to be taken straight for the exchange, so I have advised my command about it. They told me to take the bodies back to the Vojnic nevertheless and place them in a fridge and then conduct the exchange late at night the same day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you do that?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we did, but with the five that I picked up, I had only 99. So when we came to the place where the meeting was set up with the 5th Corps, they brought big trucks. We lined them up along the road, 99 on our side, they took one, put it back on the truck and they left 99 on the road. So it was 99 for 99.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to go into an entirely different area.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm just mindful of the time before embarking on a new area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. I think that would be a convenient moment. How much longer do you anticipate?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I would expect approximately 40 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll adjourn now. Mr. Lazarevic, would you please be back tomorrow morning at 9.00 --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- to continue your evidence. Thank you.
